newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania brewer in talks with Carlsberg.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania brewer in talks with Carlsberg.

text.p: Lithuania's leading brewer Utenos said on Monday that it was pursuing talks with Denmark's Carlsberg over a possible 80 to 100 million litas investment.
"We continue serious talks with Carlsberg...the potential investment for our company is worth 80 to 100 million litas," the chairman of Utenos' board Arunas Lubys told Reuters.
Lubys added that a delegation from Carlsberg was arriving today in the town of Utena, where the brewer is based.
Lubys said that a delay in the registeration of his company's shares with the securities commission had proven to be an obstacle to the Carlsberg investment.
"If our shares had been registered, the investment might have been made by now," he said.
He said the delay had been caused by a dispute with the government, which owns a 21.5 percent stake in the brewer.
Utenos earlier announced its 1996 net profit had slipped to 7.2 million litas from 7.5 million litas the previous year.

The company also said that it expects its 1997 net profit to fall further to 6.5 million litas because it plans to launch an agressive sales and marketing campaign to retain its leading hold on the Lithuanian beer market.
Lubys said that Utenos' share of the local beer market in 1996 was 35 percent.
